definition: Emergency calls received on a standard 10-digit phone line rather than through the 9-1-1 network.
The three-digit dialing code that directly connects individuals to the pre-existing National Suicide Prevention Lifeline network of crisis centers (now called the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline).
Equipment that automatically distributes incoming calls to available PSAP attendants in the order the calls are received, or queues calls until an attendant becomes available.
The world's oldest and largest not-for-profit professional organization dedicated to the enhancement of public safety communications.
nenaTerm: APCO (Association of Public Safety Communications Officials)

definition: A PSAP or dispatch center that assumes call-taking or dispatch responsibilities when another center is unavailable or overwhelmed.
The hour each day with the greatest emergency call volume at a PSAP.
A computer-based system that aids PSAP Telecommunicators by automating selected dispatching and record keeping activities.

A Functional Element concerned with the details of the management of calls. It handles all communication from the caller. It includes the interfaces, devices, and applications utilized by the Agents to handle the call.
The interval from when a call is answered until it is dispatched, or until the call is dispatchable — that is, until the telecommunicator has enough information to dispatch it.
Commission on Fire Accreditation International.
A call transfer where the transferring telecommunicator disconnects once the call is routed, without confirming the receiving party has answered.
The number of calls being handled simultaneously at a given moment. A key driver of NG9-1-1 system capacity and cost.
The total hours a telecommunicator is scheduled to work in a year, per their employment agreement.
Full-Time Equivalent. A unit that indicates the workload of an employed person.
International Academies of Emergency Dispatch.
A real-world occurrence, or event, for which one or more calls may be received.
An agreement between agencies or jurisdictions to provide assistance and resources during emergencies.
National Crime Information Center. The FBI's criminal justice information system, used by PSAPs for warrant checks, stolen vehicle lookups, and other law-enforcement queries.

Referred to as "The 9-1-1 Association", it is fully dedicated to the continued improvement and modernization of the 9-1-1 emergency communication system. NENA's approach includes research, standards development, training, education, certification, outreach, and advocacy through communication with stakeholders. As an ANSI-accredited Standards Developer, NENA works with 9-1-1 professionals, public policy leaders, emergency services and telecommunications industry partners, like-minded public safety associations, and more. Current NENA activities center on awareness, documentation, and implementation for Next Generation 9-1-1 (NG9-1-1) and international three-digit emergency communication systems. NENA's worldwide members join with the emergency response community in striving to protect human life, preserve property, and maintain the security of all communities.
Contracted hours minus vacation, training, sick leave, and other non-operational time. Represents actual time available for call handling.

An IP-based system comprised of hardware, software, data, and operational policies and procedures that: (A) provides standardized interfaces from emergency call and message services to support emergency communications; (B) processes all types of emergency calls, including voice, data, and multimedia information; (C) acquires and integrates additional emergency call data useful to call routing and handling; (D) delivers the emergency calls, messages, and data to the appropriate public safety answering point and other appropriate emergency entities; (E) supports data or video communications needs for coordinated incident response and management.
Next Generation Core Services. The IP-based infrastructure that routes 9-1-1 calls in an NG9-1-1 environment.
A physical or virtual entity where 9-1-1 calls are delivered by the 9-1-1 Service Provider.
A process taken to ensure that standards and procedures are adhered to and that delivered products or services meet performance requirements.
An organized system that assesses and evaluates the process to improve the quality of services provided.
A transmission on a radio channel, typically initiated by pressing the push-to-talk button. Counted as a workload unit in dispatch operations.
Request for Assistance. A request from one agency to another for support or resources.
A text transmission that is character at a time, as in TTY. Technology that allows consumers to send and receive IETF RFC 4103 text characters, as they are typed, as well as audio simultaneously.
Emergency messaging via satellite, available on certain mobile devices when cellular service is unavailable.

A contract between a service provider (either internal or external) and the end user that defines the level of service expected from the service provider. SLAs are output-based in that their purpose is specifically to define what the customer will receive.
A feature that allows the PSAP Telecommunicator to redirect a 9-1-1 call to another location.

A device capable of information interchange between compatible units using a dial-up or private-line telephone network and VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) connections as the transmission mediums. ASCII tones or Baudot codes are used by these units (per EIA PN-1663).
localNote: Related term: TDD (Telecommunications Device for the Deaf).

definition: A call transfer where the transferring telecommunicator remains on the line until the receiving party answers and the handoff is complete.
The number of hours in a standard work year used for FTE calculations. Common conventions are 2,080 hours (5 x 8-hour shifts) and 2,184 hours (12-hour / "Pittman" schedule).
Post-call work performed by the telecommunicator after the call ends, before they are available for the next call. May include documentation, follow-up calls, or system updates.
